article: On Thursday, the U.S. House of Representatives voted 269-152 to reject the Net Neutrality Amendment to the COPE Act. The amendment sought to require broadband providers to treat all data equally, specifying a duty not to block, impair, degrade, discriminate against, or interfere with access to lawful content, applications, or services. Its passage would have prevented companies such as AT&T, Verizon, and Comcast from charging content providers like Google, Yahoo, Amazon, or eBay for priority network access. House Minority Leader Nancy Pelosi argued that additional fees would burden small web-based businesses and hamper noncommercial communications. Phone companies and Congressional allies argued the restrictions would discourage investment in network upgrades. Democrats largely supported the amendment, with 140 voting in favor and 58 against, while 11 Republicans voted for it and 211 against. The COPE Act, designed to make it easier for telecommunications companies to offer cable TV service and strengthen competition, passed by a 321-101 vote the same day. Proponents said it would lower high-speed Internet prices by enabling providers to bundle phone, data, video, and mobile services. It was the first major telecommunications bill before Congress in over a decade. The bill is due to be discussed next in the Senate.

article: A pledge to double the wild tiger population on the continent to seven thousand by 2022 was made on Friday by ministers from thirteen Asian countries. The meeting was partially organized by the Global Tiger Initiative, a coalition within the World Bank, as well as the Smithsonian Institution and various conservation groups. It was noted by meeting host Suwit Khunkitti, Thailand's minister of natural resources and environment, that there were 100,000 tigers across range countries 100 years ago, compared to about 3,500 today. According to the World Wildlife Fund (WWF), tiger numbers have declined due to poaching. The animals live in only seven percent of the territory they occupied a hundred years ago, according to Voice of America. WWF representative Michael Baltzer said it was important to act during the Year of the Tiger. Global Tiger Initiative program director Keshav Varma said saving the tiger also preserves habitat for other species and draws attention to issues including encroachment and corruption.

No gender gap exists in attendance for the richest 20% of Indian families, but males outnumber females 5 to 1 among the poorest 20%. India reduced average children per woman from six to three in 35 years, compared with 100 years in the United States. India's maternal mortality rate is six times that of Sri Lanka. article: U.S. District Judge Stein ruled that the use of a 25-second clip from John Lennon's song "Imagine" in a film critical of religion is likely defensible under the fair use doctrine. On May 19, a preliminary injunction was issued preventing distribution of the film. On June 2, Judge Stein ruled that the fair use defense would likely succeed and lifted the injunction, writing that "the fair use of a copyrighted work for the purposes of criticism and commentary is not an infringement of copyright." "Expelled" is a contentious documentary claiming that intelligent design proponents are being suppressed by the scientific community. It has received sharp criticism from scientists and film critics and has faced additional copyright claims over animated sequences resembling "The Inner Life of the Cell," produced by XVIVO and Harvard University.
